speaker: Doctor
text: I cannot diagnose pyelonephritis based on a pruritic rash and respiratory symptoms, as this is clinically inconsistent. I need to examine the patient's rash and ask about their medical history to determine the correct diagnosis.

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The facial rash sparing the perioral area is highly suggestive of Erythema Marginatum. REQUEST IMAGES: Rash distribution and morphology.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a prodrome followed by a facial rash sparing the mouth and then a widespread rash is classic for Fifth Disease (Erythema Infectiosum). DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum
